study type: Institution based unmatched case control study
cohort: 444 postpartum mothers (111 cases with puerperal sepsis and 333 controls without)
finding: Rural residence, no ANC follow-up, prolonged rupture of membranes, prolonged labor, frequent vaginal examinations, cesarean section, and no PNC follow-up were identified as determinants of puerperal sepsis.
mod_finding: Cesarean section mode of delivery was identified as a determinant factor for puerperal sepsis.
